Physics hand-checked: regelation is the melting of ice under increased pressure and its re-freezing when the pressure is removed, because the melting point of ice falls as the pressure on it rises — ice under pressure sits above its own melting point and melts, and releasing the pressure raises the melting point again so the water re-freezes.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The phenomenon
lines: Regelation is the melting of ice under
again once the pressure is removed.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say ice melts under pressure and freezes again once the pressure is removed.
steps.why: This one sentence names the whole cycle — melting under load, then re-freezing the instant the load is taken away — which is the phenomenon regelation names.
common_mistakes: Describing only the melting and leaving out that the ice freezes again when the pressure is removed.

recall.must_convey: That regelation is the melting of ice under increased pressure and its freezing again when the pressure is removed.
accept: melts under pressure and freezes again
pressure melts it, removing it re-freezes
reject: melting point falls as pressure rises

steps.memory_tip: Regelation: melt under pressure, freeze again once it is gone.

steps.label: The reason
lines: It happens because the melting point of
ice falls as the pressure on it rises.
Ice under pressure is then above its own
melting point and melts. Removing the
pressure raises the melting point again,
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say the melting point of ice falls as pressure rises, and rises again when pressure is removed.
steps.why: Most substances have a melting point that rises with pressure; ice is one of the few whose melting point falls with pressure, and that reversal is the reason pressure alone can melt it and releasing pressure can freeze it again.
common_mistakes: Saying only that pressure melts ice, without saying the melting point of ice falls as pressure rises.

recall.must_convey: That the melting point of ice falls as pressure rises, so pressure melts it and removing the pressure lets it re-freeze.
accept: melting point falls as pressure rises
pressure lowers the melting point of ice
ice sits above its melting point under pressure
reject: freezes again when pressure is removed

steps.memory_tip: Ice is unusual: pressure LOWERS its melting point, instead of raising it.

insider_note: Regelation is two ideas together: the melting-and-re-freezing cycle, and the reason for it — the melting point of ice falling as the pressure on it rises. A complete answer states both.
